lessons.title: Maps Show Places
lessons.objective: I know a map shows where things are.

teach.text: A map is a picture of a place from above.
A globe is a map shaped like a ball — it shows the whole Earth.

questions.prompt: A globe is shaped like a...
Which one shows the whole Earth?

lessons.title: Land and Water
lessons.objective: I can tell land from water on a map.

teach.text: On maps, blue usually means water and green or brown means land.
Big areas of salty water are oceans. Big areas of land are continents.

questions.prompt: What color usually shows water on a map?
A very big area of salt water is an...
A huge area of land is a...

lessons.title: Continents and Oceans
lessons.objective: I know Earth has 7 continents and big oceans.

teach.text: Earth has 7 continents, like North America and Africa.
It also has large oceans, like the Pacific and Atlantic.

questions.prompt: How many continents does Earth have?

lessons.title: The United States
lessons.objective: I know basic facts about the USA.

teach.text: The United States has 50 states and a capital city.
The capital is Washington, D.C. Each state also has its own capital.

questions.prompt: How many states are in the USA?
What is the capital of the United States?
Which state is the largest by land?
